name: Shurink

lead: Shurink is a Korean HIFU treatment for non-surgical skin tightening. It is popular for jawline definition and V-line shaping.
A session takes roughly 20 to 30 minutes with numbing cream, and clinics describe no downtime.

paras: Focused ultrasound delivers heat to a chosen depth beneath the skin, which is thought to prompt tightening and a lifted look [1].
Clinic pages do not list side effects; a provider can describe them. Effects are not permanent and treatment is done by trained clinicians.

angle.text: Shurink aims focused ultrasound energy at a chosen depth to tighten and lift. People use it for jawline definition, V-line shaping and firmer skin without surgery or recovery time.

lead: Shurink is a Korean high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) skin-tightening treatment, offered in clinics as a non-surgical lift for the face and jawline. Clinic pages describe it as using focused ultrasound to tighten sagging skin and improve elasticity, and people seek it for a more defined jawline, a V-line face shape, firmer skin and more balanced facial contours.[1]

A session is described as lasting about 20 to 30 minutes with topical numbing cream and no hospital stay or recovery period.[1] A consultation sets the energy level and number of shots for each person's concerns, with the energy aimed at a chosen skin layer.[1] The name is used by Korean clinics, and the treatment is listed in some places as marketed under the Ultraformer III name.

HIFU in general uses non-ionising ultrasound waves focused on a small target to heat tissue there; medical uses documented for the technology include essential tremor and tumour treatment.[2] The clinic page cited here does not present clinical study data or registered before-and-after photographs for Shurink.[1]

paras: Clinics describe designing each session individually, choosing the energy level and number of shots for the person's concerns, with energy aimed at the target skin layer.[1] Claimed effects include lifting and firming, better skin elasticity, a 'natural V-line effect', definition of a faint jawline and balancing of asymmetrical facial contours.[1]

High-intensity focused ultrasound is an incisionless technique in which ultrasonic waves are focused so that tissue at the focal point is heated; the general Wikipedia article says the focus can reach 65 to 85 degrees Celsius for medical ablation, and that tissue heated above 60 degrees for more than a second is irreversibly damaged.[2] Aesthetic devices use lower, targeted settings aimed at skin and the layer beneath, which clinics say prompts tightening; the Wikipedia article itself documents only medical uses, such as essential tremor, tumours and kidney stones.[2]

The clinic page does not list side effects, and says treatment is individualised after consultation.[1] Effects of HIFU skin tightening are generally described as gradual and not permanent, and the procedure is performed by clinicians.
